slides.headline: Amazon Mobilizes Ring. Privacy Questions Follow.
slides.subheadline: Roaming cameras promise wider coverage. Cloud access complicates their privacy assurances.

telemetry.label: Ring Rover Cam
telemetry.qualification: Business patrol robot available for preorder.

slides.svgBlueprint: Portrait 1080×1350. Use the supplied palette throughout the carousel. Place Custom Brand above a thin orange rule; kicker beneath. Anchor two price badges along the bottom and the issue badge at the top right. No schematic, arrows, or callout boxes.

slides.headline: The Announcement Outruns The Arrival
slides.subheadline: Amazon has announced both devices; their shipping dates remain ahead.

items.title: ANNOUNCED
items.body: Amazon introduces Ring Robotics: a flying home camera and a wheeled business patrol robot.

items.title: ROVER SHIPPING TARGET
items.body: Ring Rover Cam shipping is scheduled; preorders are open.

items.title: DRONE SHIPPING TARGET
items.body: Ring Drone Cam awaits FCC authorization; offering it for sale or lease remains prohibited.

slides.svgBlueprint: Portrait 1080×1350 with 72px safe margins. Set a 60px headline above a left-aligned vertical spine. Stack three spacious milestones chronologically downward. Use one solid orange node for the announcement and two outlined nodes for future shipping targets. Dates are 36px numerical badges; bodies are 30px. End the drone milestone with a small outlined regulatory gate, not an approval checkmark.

slides.headline: Uncompromised Privacy, Connected By Design
slides.subheadline: Amazon pairs its privacy assurance with cloud navigation and subscription-dependent scheduling.

items.title: THE ASSURANCE
items.body: Amazon promises “privacy and security without compromise”: recording indicators and Throw Away the Key Encryption.

items.title: THE ARCHITECTURE
items.body: AI Pilot combines cameras, vision models, sensors and cloud processing; setup creates indoor floor plans.

items.title: THE SUBSCRIPTION
items.body: Scheduled drone flights and Rover patrols require a compatible Ring Protect plan.

slides.svgBlueprint: Portrait 1080×1350. Place a broad assurance card beneath the 60px headline, followed by two narrower cards stacked with alternating horizontal offsets. Use Surface fills, Ink text and orange clause markers. A restrained cloud contour sits behind the architecture card; a calendar outline marks scheduling. Keep bodies at 30px and avoid decorative numbers or unsupported subscription prices.

slides.headline: Deleting Keys Doesn't Eliminate Access
slides.subheadline: EFF's September 11, 2026 analysis challenges TAKE, not the robots' navigation.

items.title: THE ACCESS WINDOW
items.body: Ring's cloud receives video keys for processing, then deletes its copy after 24 hours.

items.title: THE RETURN PATH
items.body: Later playback or smart features can return keys; EFF says TAKE is not end-to-end encryption.

slides.svgBlueprint: Portrait 1080×1350. Divide the content field into two tall panels beneath a shared 60px headline. Left: a key inside a cloud contour, with the 24 hours badge at 52px. Right: a returning arrow carrying the same key toward the cloud. Use an orange divider and generous negative space. Label the right path with words, not an invented duration. Bodies remain 30px; diagrams show access mechanics, not a proven breach.

slides.headline: A Recording Light Isn't An Answer
slides.subheadline: Expanded visibility demands accountable access—not merely cameras that can navigate indoors.

items.title: DOCUMENTED / AMAZON
items.body: Amazon specifies cloud-assisted navigation and visible recording indicators; these are commitments, not independent performance findings.

items.title: CONTESTED / EFF
items.body: Ring reports independent security testing; EFF seeks infrastructure-wide auditing of TAKE's privacy claims.

items.title: VERDICT / STILL OPEN
items.body: Indicators disclose recording, not access. Can independently verified safeguards match the cameras' expanded indoor reach?
